title: Sort Numbers Without the Built-In
statement:
Given an integer array nums, return a new array with the same numbers in ascending order. Duplicates stay; nothing is removed.

The point is to write the sort yourself: do not call Array.prototype.sort, sorted or any other library sort. Your sort must run in O(n log n) time or better, so a simple quadratic sort will be too slow on the largest inputs.

examples.why: Both copies of -2 are kept, and negative numbers come before zero.
Numbers are compared by value, not as text. A string comparison would put 10 before 2.
A single number is already sorted.

hints: Splitting the array in half is easy. If both halves were already sorted, how fast could you combine them?
Merging two sorted lists is a two-pointer walk: always take the smaller front item. That is O(n) per level, and halving gives log n levels.
The values live in a small fixed range, so counting how often each value appears and writing them back in order also works, in O(n + range).

explain.intuition:
Merge sort is divide and conquer. Sorting one number is free. Two sorted lists can be merged in linear time by repeatedly taking the smaller of their two front items. So: split in half, sort each half the same way, merge. Each level of splitting does O(n) merging work in total, and there are about log n levels, giving O(n log n) in every case, including already-sorted and reverse-sorted input.

When the values sit in a known small range, like here, counting sort skips comparisons altogether: count each value, then write the values out in order as many times as they were counted. It is the same idea as building a histogram and reading it from left to right.
steps: If the array has at most one element, return it.
Split it at the middle and sort each half recursively.
Merge: keep an index into each half, push the smaller front value, advance that index.
When one half runs out, append the rest of the other half.
pitfalls: Writing a quadratic sort (bubble, insertion, selection). It is correct but times out on 50 000 numbers.
Quick sort with a fixed first or last pivot. Sorted input or many equal values make it quadratic. Pick a random pivot and split three ways.
Forgetting to copy the leftover tail of one half after the merge loop ends.

solutions.title: Insertion sort
solutions.idea: Grow a sorted prefix one element at a time, shifting bigger values right to make room. Fine for small inputs, quadratic in general.

solutions.title: Merge sort
solutions.idea: Sort each half recursively, then merge the two sorted halves with two pointers.

solutions.title: Counting sort
solutions.idea: Values are between -50 000 and 50 000. Count each value, then write them back in increasing order.

followups: Sort in place with O(1) extra memory and O(n log n) worst case. Which algorithm gives you both?
